bindingDecisions: Document copilot is a document-scoped side inspector, not a standalone chat pasted beside the editor.
AI context must be explicit and server-authorized: current document id, title, revision, selected blocks if available, and a bounded text snapshot.
Provider keys remain server-owned; the browser only sees provider config views and conversation/run DTOs.
Task21a must not auto-apply, rewrite, insert, or mutate the document. Answers are advisory/copyable only.
Reuse the existing AI conversation/run streaming stack instead of building a second provider pipeline.
Respect Task20m: document body stays clean; copilot UI lives in the inspector and uses mature side-panel visual rhythm.
preparation.rootProblem: After Task20m the document editor is usable, but the AI area is still a placeholder that sends users to standalone chat and has no trustworthy document-scoped context contract.
preparation.firstImplementationPriority: Replace DeferredDocumentAI with a real document copilot baseline that captures explicit current-document context, streams via the existing AI conversation API, and never writes back automatically.

noSuccessWithout: Notebook and Project document editors show the same document-scoped copilot panel in the inspector
Copilot panel displays the exact current document context being sent: document title, id/type, revision/base revision, and bounded content summary or selected-block summary
Sending a message uses existing server-owned AI provider configuration and existing conversation streaming endpoints
The browser never receives provider API keys, encrypted keys, raw provider payload secrets, signed attachment URLs, object keys, or storage secrets
AI responses are advisory only; there is no auto apply, auto insert, auto rewrite, or silent document mutation in Task21a
Draft autosave/formal save/revision conflict behavior from the document editor remains unchanged
Provider-missing, stream error, abort/cancel, empty document, and read-only document states are visible and tested
Standalone AI chat remains usable or is deliberately not touched
Human manual review verifies document-context display, send/stream behavior, no writeback, and Notebook/Project parity
forbiddenCompletionClaims: A chat box appears, therefore document copilot is done
The model probably knows the document without showing context to the user
Auto-inserting AI output is acceptable in the first copilot baseline
Leaking provider keys or signed attachment URLs to the browser is acceptable for convenience
Only Notebook was checked, therefore Project parity is assumed

environment.browserDevice: remote browser via LAN review stack

manualReview.summary: User confirmed provider configuration and successful AI conversation in the document copilot. The remaining concern is visual quality: current side-panel and workspace AI chat feel like control panels rather than mature chat surfaces, so that work is split into Task21b.
passedChecks: Provider configuration succeeded with server-owned keys.
Document copilot could send a prompt and receive an AI response.
Task21a automated and finish checks covered provider-key safety, document no-writeback, and focused regression coverage.
Manual review identified visual/chat-surface quality as the next product problem rather than a Task21a functional blocker.
manualReview.remainingFollowUp: Task21b must refactor AI chat side panel and full workspace chat into mature conversation surfaces, preserving Task21a safety and no-writeback contracts.
